messages:
Evelyn: Quick idea dump: we should add a quota-aware bucketing layer between sampler and orchestrator. Goal: avoid a single model flood eating bench capacity and starving critical canaries. Thoughts?

Ajay: Sounds sensible. Do you mean per-model quotas, or per-corpus quotas?

Evelyn: Per-model+per-policy. Example: model X gets 100 smoke slots/hour, 10 full slots/hour. Sampler tags BatchDescriptor with bucket_id. Orchestrator enforces quotas.

Leah: +1. Also want soft-buckets for exploration: allow temporary burst that auto-throttles if it causes queue pressure.

Tom: Implementation note: orchestrator should expose a token-bucket for each bucket_id. Sampler obtains tokens via a cheap lease call: /lease?bucket=b123&count=10. If lease fails sampler can fallback to lower-priority buckets.

Ravi: What about cross-tenant quotas for Dedicated vs Hosted? Dedicated customers shouldn't be impacted by global sampler churn. We need deployment_mode-aware quotas.

Evelyn: Right — bucket key = <deployment_mode>::<policy>::<model_family>. Default fallback to global if not set.

Nora: Observability ask: when quota denies a sample, emit denial_reason + suggested retry_after. Otherwise folks will get puzzled why their canary didn't run.

benchbot: quota-event: bucket:hosted::stratA::gptx-3, action:lease_granted, tokens:8, remaining:92

Ajay: Canary scheduling: we should schedule stable canaries on a low-latency fastpath and shadow-run against a larger distributed cohort. Canary hints: {strict:true, shadow: true, sample_expiry: 60000}.

Leah: For canary quality checks, define auto-rollback triggers: e.g., if delta Rouge/EM/LLM-score > threshold AND > p95 latency, then flag. Rollback shouldn't be automatic for golden samples without human signoff, but for smoke canaries we can auto-abort rollout.

Tom: Agree. Add signal sources: eval metrics, token-level quality drift, and traffic error-rate. Rollback policy should be a policy object referenced by rollout_id.

Ravi: Edge case: sampler picks heavy long-run samples but orchestrator only has smoke slots. We should provide a bijection: sampler receives a quota_hint API telling approximate wait or bucket capacity so it can choose alternatives.

Evelyn: Good point. Lease API can return {granted:false, next_available_ms: 120000, alternative_buckets: [b-smoke-lowercost]}. Sampler can decide to downgrade or requeue.

Nora: Security/regulatory: for private deployments, the lease API must be reachable locally only. Do not route quotas through central multi-tenant service. Local policy agent should implement same semantics and sync policies from central controller.

benchbot: policy-sync: central->local agent applied. diff: quotas updated for gptx-3: smoke +10%.

Ajay: Batching: orchestrator should be quota-aware when aggregating requests into batches. Don't mix buckets in a single GPU batch unless QoS is compatible. That prevents a low-priority long job from dragging a high-priority smoke.

Leah: Suggest batch affinity: only co-schedule descriptors where hints.qos_group == X. If different but compatible (e.g., different seqlens) we can pack if all have same priority and no strict hints.

Tom: Small config snippet for lease endpoint:
```
POST /lease
body: { bucket: "hosted::stratA::gptx-3", tokens: 8 }
resp: { granted: true, tokens: 8, ttl_ms: 60000, remaining: 92 }
```

Ravi: Failure handling: if orchestrator can't honor a leased token because payload fetch fails, it should release token with reason and sampler can requeue or pick alternate sample. Also record a "lease_lost" event for debugging.

Evelyn: Next: I'll add quota layer section to RFC and a short sequence diagram. Ajay, can you own the lease API PoC? Leah, can you adjust sampler to use alternative buckets and shadow behavior?

Ajay: I got the lease PoC. Will return a minimal HTTP mock and a small token-bucket impl.

Leah: I'll update sampler PoC to prefer strict canaries and gracefully downgrade to alternate buckets.

Evelyn: Thanks. Let's reconvene after PoCs. I'll open RFC draft and attach this thread. :raised_hands:
